Riley (Customer): Hey team — over the last 30m our calls to /v1/rerank are returning 429s intermittently. Sample response: {\"error\":\"Rate limit exceeded\",\"code\":429}. We're sending batches of 64 items per request at ~250 rps. Any quick help?

Maya (Support): Sorry about that — we'll investigate. Can you paste a sanitized curl + headers and a few request-ids from the responses? Do you see a Retry-After header coming back? I'll open a ticket and loop in eng.

Riley (Customer): Pasting sanitized payload + headers:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n -d '{"query":"best hotels in SF","candidates":[...64 items...],"batch_size":64}'\n
Response headers we get: x-ratelimit-limit: 1000\nx-ratelimit-remaining: 0\nx-ratelimit-reset: 2053123500\nretry-after: 3\nrequest-id: req_8a3f9b
```

SupportBot: Ticket created INC-2025-789 and assigned to eng-runtime + quota-team :ticket:

Maya (Support): I see a spike from your API key around 14:05 UTC correlated with the 429s. Did you recently change job schedule or concurrency?

Riley (Customer): We kicked off a nightly bulk re-rank at 14:00 that fans out into ~200 concurrent clients, each sending batches of 64. We assumed larger batch -> fewer requests, but looks like we hit a per-second concurrency cap.

Ethan (SRE): Confirming from the rate-limiter logs: your key exceeded the per-route QPS cap for /v1/rerank which triggers burst backpressure. The limiter emitted 429s with Retry-After values between 2 and 5s. Short-term mitigations: implement client-side concurrency limit, respect Retry-After, add exponential backoff with jitter. We can provide a temporary quota bump if needed.

Lina (Eng Runtime): We reproduced this with a small script: 5 parallel workers + batch_size=64 => consistent 429s. Lowering batch_size to 16-32 or reducing parallelism under ~20 workers removes the 429s. Rerank has both per-token and per-request shaping; large batches can still spike concurrent compute and trigger per-route defenses.

Maya (Support): Action items for Riley: 1) implement exponential backoff (start 200ms, factor 2, jitter) and honor Retry-After 2) reduce batch_size to 16-32 for the nightly run 3) stagger job start across hosts 4) send the exact request-ids/timestamps in the ticket so eng can stitch logs.

Riley (Customer): Will do — can you also escalate for a temporary quota bump? This is impacting a paying customer's SLA.

Maya (Support): Escalation requested — quota-team & sales notified in INC-2025-789. We can provision a 24h burst window while you refactor. For long-term sustained throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity or an increased per-route quota (sales will follow up).

Ethan (SRE): Additional suggestion: for very high-volume re-rank workflows consider embeddings + local re-rank hybrid (embed once, do lightweight similarity locally) to reduce pressure on the rerank endpoint.

Lina (Eng Runtime): We'll also check kernel scheduling logs and see if a different quantization/model variant would reduce CPU/GPU contention for large batches. I'll post follow-up in the ticket with repro traces.

Riley (Customer): Thanks everyone — implementing throttling now and will update INC-2025-789 with timestamps and request-ids. Appreciate the quick help :pray:

Maya (Support): Thanks — marking this thread as escalated. We'll keep the ticket open until quota/mitigations are confirmed.
